chunks: And in the narration of 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far, he said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a man who had sexual intercourse with the concubine of his wife without her permission, saying: 'He bears the same penalty as the fornicator, but he is not stoned, and the punishment of the fornicator does not apply except if he commits adultery with a free Muslim woman.'

key_terms.فَجَرَ: To have sexual intercourse / commit fornication

ai.seo_question: What is the legal penalty for a man having sex with his wife's concubine without her permission according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that a man having intercourse with his wife's concubine without her consent incurs the penalty of a fornicator (fajir) but is exempt from stoning (rajm). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the hadd of rajm is strictly reserved for free Muslim women, whereas concubines, being slaves, receive the lesser penalty of flogging, reflecting the nuanced application of Quranic verses on zina in classical fiqh.
